notes: v229 — AUTOSTART-FIRED-ON-UNSELECTED-DAY (owner, Fri Oct 23, 2026 ~10:15 MDT, his screen recording): his job was CANCELLED; before falling asleep he deleted today's dispatch in the app and confirmed the Auto-start card — enabled, 8:00 AM, Fri OFF, and the card's own line said "Today: no auto-start scheduled". On waking, the tracker was RUNNING, "Counting from 8:00 AM" — a session existed for a day that was never scheduled. ROOT CAUSE (js/app.js only): the start decision at boot/resume was taken on this device's LOCAL store BEFORE the boot's first cloud pull settled. His edits were saved to the account; the phone's local copy still held the pre-edit state (Friday selected, the deleted dispatch still in it), so the boot checkAutoStart started a session from the stale read — anchored 8:00, exactly as designed — and seconds later the pull settled the store to the state his card displayed, with nothing able to un-start the session. The native arm decision (App.armNativeDay) was placed from the same first read. THE FIX: while a signed-in pull for this boot is outstanding, the START and the ARM decision wait for it (one latch per boot; the waiter settles on pull success, pull failure, or its 30s timeout — offline, the local copy is the only truth the phone has and the start proceeds on it, backdated as always; local mode never waits). When the pull settles, the check and the arm re-run once on the settled store — the same store the card reads, so card and engine can never again disagree about whether today was scheduled. The day-watch arming, the day gate, the precedence (override > dispatch > setting) and the anchored-start law are untouched: movement still only arms, and a session's start is still the plan time, never the wake.
